headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 7 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.56 (95% CI: 0.42–0.76), suggesting that vitamin_b6 is associated with a lower risk of breast cancer. However, this association should be interpreted with caution, as there was substantial between-study heterogeneity (I² = 72.15%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
